verdict.line: You lose if you trade autos into Gnar's range and Hop-bounce poke before level 6; you win if you farm patiently, land Wither, and bring Fury of the Sands into fights from level 6 onward.

brief.thesis: Gnar's Boomerang Throw (Q, 1100 range) outranges your 255-range Siphoning Strike entirely, and his Hop (E) bounces off your champion for extra distance, which is exactly why he holds the lane and solo-kill edge in the data. But your Q stacks are permanent and uncapped, and once Wither and Fury of the Sands come online at 6 you gain the only tools in this matchup that stop his kiting — which is why the 1662-game head-to-head still sits at 52.2% in your favor despite losing lane.

theirWindow.what: Gnar free-pokes with Boomerang Throw and Hop (E, 475 range) bounces off you for extra poke while you have no way to close distance. If his Rage gauge maxes and he transforms, Mega Gnar's W (Wallop) becomes a ground-smash stun and his E becomes an AoE landing instead of a bounce — do not stand and trade into that transformation.

yourWindow.what: Once Wither (W, 700 range) lands on Gnar, its decelerating Move and Attack Speed slow blunts his kite tools long enough to close the gap. Commit with Fury of the Sands active for the bonus Health, Attack Range, and the max-Health drain into bonus damage.

start.why: 51.7% win rate over 1475 games — the flat damage reduction on the first hit each 3 seconds eats into Gnar's poke autos and Boomerang Throw chip damage while you farm with Q.

boots.why: 51.6% win rate, 43.9% pick rate — the ability haste shortens Siphoning Strike and Wither cooldowns, letting you stack Q faster and threaten Wither more often through the poke phase.

core.why: 56.3% win rate path — the biggest single damage and tempo spike, giving you the stats to start winning extended trades once Wither lands.
Armor and attack speed slow punish Gnar for sticking in melee range to auto you, and the cooldown reduction keeps Wither up more often.
Heal and shield power amplify your Soul Eater lifesteal and Fury of the Sands' health drain, turning extended all-ins into sustained wins.

situational.when: gnar is building into crit or lifesteal and out-damaging your sustain
you need more move speed to catch his hop-kiting before fights start
you want the wave-clear and slow proc earlier instead of trinity force's full spike

runes.keystoneWhy: The heal and move speed on landing attacks or abilities offset the chip damage from Boomerang Throw and let you close small gaps during the poke phase instead of just absorbing it.

summoners.why: 52.6% win rate combo — Ghost is the only reliable way to stick onto a kiting ranged bully long enough to land Wither, and Flash covers you if Gnar transforms and commits an all-in before you're ready.

playing.title: Farm with Q, don't trade
playing.detail: Use Siphoning Strike only to secure minions before level 6. Trading autos into Gnar's longer range and Hop bounce is a losing exchange.

playing.title: Respect the Rage gauge
playing.detail: Track Gnar's Rage bar all lane. Near max, he's about to transform, and Mega Gnar's Wallop (W) becomes a stun while his Crunch (E) becomes an AoE landing instead of a bounce — back off rather than stand in it.

playing.title: Hold engages until 6
playing.detail: Without Fury of the Sands you have no way to close distance on a kiting ranged champion, so don't commit before level 6 no matter how low he pushes his wave.

playing.title: Wither before you commit
playing.detail: Land Wither (700 range) on Gnar before diving. It's the only tool that decelerates his Move and Attack Speed enough to stop his Boomerang-and-Hop kite once you're in range.

playing.title: Spirit Fire extended trades
playing.detail: Drop Spirit Fire (650 range, 12s cooldown) under Gnar in any stand-and-fight moment. The Armor reduction matters most once your stacked Q is dealing real damage.

playing.title: Save R to flip all-ins
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands' health drain and bonus Health/Attack Range turn a losing 1v1 into a win from level 6 on. Hold it for when Gnar transforms or commits his Hop engage.

playing.title: Teleport back, don't flash in
playing.detail: If you're running Teleport, use it to return to lane after shoving or recalling, not as an engage tool. This matchup rewards patience, not forced fights.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the tactical reading of ability tells, timing windows, and trade patterns is this brief's own analysis.

stats.opponentTip: Keep some distance to avoid being kited by Mini Gnar while you farm. Keep your [Q] stacks up and wait for an opportunity to go in post-level 6.
